section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` The failed devotion was planted at {settlement} to soften the ground; the pilgrims coming back down the {route} contradicted it plainly and went on contradicting it; and the claim was never pressed, because the ground it wanted was never soft.

section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` {faction} put the word of {counterpart}'s plenty on the road deliberately, and the road did the rest without being asked twice.

section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` The plenty at {counterpart} was planted by {faction} and cost what a plant costs; the rush arrived well before any correction could; and the letters that finally came back are that correction, late, and the towns that emptied for it are not refilling on anybody's apology.

section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` The one account out of {settlement} that has been true in every particular is {npc}'s, and {npc} has been handing the same truth to {counterpart}.

section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` {settlement} sent the one envoy to save the cost; the account that came back was clean, complete and exactly what {counterpart} wished {settlement} to hold; and the hurried seat has the treaty it paid for.

section: §1.2 — THE FAITH, POPULATION AND INFORMATION QUARTER (CPL-11 … CPL-20, both directions)
text: `[dm-only]` The plant was placed at {settlement} to move a seat, and it moved one; the exposure came later and cited the condition still standing on the record; and the hand that placed it is entered on the same beat, which is why that beat reads the way it does.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
text: The first demand was small and {settlement} met it, and the season was quiet. The second came in the same hand, larger, and was met too. What {counterpart}'s book records is not a grudge but a return on a venture, and the entries are getting bolder. {settlement}'s granary carries the whole education.

section: §1.3 — CPL-21, THE STORY CANON AND THE SIGNATURE STORIES
text: The lens belongs to the town and not to the god: the bad season is read as the withdrawal and the good one as its return, and the record says which reading was made, by whom, and in what week.

section: §1.4a THE WAR CHAINS (war → war)
text: *(HEADLINE — appended at the completion pass, 2026-08-03, per the frequency-scaled floor; numbering append-only)* The ledger against {counterpart} was long before it was loud. The {settlement} market could recite it before the council read it out.

section: §1.4a THE WAR CHAINS (war → war)
text: *[dm-only]* The covert road was quieter. {npc} carried {settlement}'s own parlay to the other side while every panel still showed the tie sound, and {counterpart}'s court bought no warning because it had no reason to think warning worth buying. The tie went on looking healthy until the week it did not.

section: §1.4a THE WAR CHAINS (war → war)
text: *[dm-only]* The charge was built out of a telling. Word of the razing reached {faction}'s hall at the road's speed and the casus was entered on what that hall believed had happened, which is the road by which a razing nobody committed can arm a war, and why the receipt names what was believed and who carried it in.

section: §1.4c THE FAITH CHAINS (faith → faith)
text: *[dm-only]* Tolerance did at {settlement} what the constables could not: the rite was left alone until there was nobody left who thought it worth keeping.

section: §1.4c THE FAITH CHAINS (faith → faith)
text: *[dm-only]* The suppression did not scatter them. A share of {creed}'s faithful went to the cellars and took the vessels with them; {npc} keeps a list of who still comes and keeps it where it will not be found; the words are said over a table and a handful answer them; the keeper who could not stay took the {route} out, and the wanderers' register carries that name now. The public record shows {creed} extinguished at {settlement}. {band} know better, and have known since the doors were barred.

section: §1.4d THE POPULATION CHAINS (pop → pop)
text: *[dm-only]* The wealth of {counterpart} was put about deliberately: {faction} wanted the road full, {house} planted the word in {settlement} and did not plant it for nothing, and the column is walking exactly where {faction} would have it and cannot know that. The cost of the word is in {house}'s book, under a heading that means nothing to a clerk.

section: §1.4d THE POPULATION CHAINS (pop → pop)
text: *[dm-only]* The word was false when it was planted and has since come nearly true, which was nobody's design. {counterpart} keeps the houses raised for the ones who did not stay; {settlement} keeps the story about who first said it; and neither town's version has the buyer in it.

section: §1.4d THE POPULATION CHAINS (pop → pop)
text: {settlement} keeps the going to {counterpart} as an errand it ordered rather than a loss it took; there is a return expected on it, and the town has not forgotten to expect it.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* The weakness {faction} marched on was true in one ledger only, and that ledger had been paid for.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* {faction} bought its picture of {counterpart}'s strength from {house} {timeband_since}, and put a column on the {route} road without ever seeking a second reading.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* Coin crossed a table at {settlement} and a telling about {counterpart} went out under {house}'s seal. It arrived slowly, the way true things do, and was taken for one; {timeband_since} it was quoted in {faction}'s council as common knowledge, with nobody able to recall who had brought it in. The commission is discharged in full. The mark bought the story, and then bought a war with it.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* Two courts, two bluffs, one war neither wanted. {settlement} reckoned {counterpart}'s garrison at a strength {counterpart} had invented, and {counterpart} returned the favour; each was certain of the other's weakness and each was the author of it. The tellings expired {band} apart in {season}, and it was the gap between those two expiries, and nothing wiser, that decided whether this was a scare or a war.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* {faction} has a courier it trusts and {house} has a courier it owns, and they are the same man.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* The channel was theirs before the errand was. {npc} carried {faction}'s cargo off the {route} road to {house} first and to {counterpart} after, and the second telling was not the first; the detour cost a leg and the leg shows, because the packet arrived late and altered. When the seat sent two and read them together, the divergence sat exactly where the detour had been, and the name that came out of that reading was {npc}'s.

section: §1.4e THE INFORMATION CHAINS (info → info)
text: *[dm-only]* The engagement closed, and the patron's side of it closed too: {house}'s book shows a courier withdrawn and {faction}'s shows one gone quiet, and only one of those two is a decision. Neither book says which.

section: §1.4f THE GRAMMAR CHAINS (grammar → grammar)
text: *[dm-only]* On every surface a free eye can reach it reads honored. {settlement} has sent less than it swore through {timeband_span}, and {counterpart}'s watchers sit too far off to weigh it. The default is real, the detection never came, and the pact will end in good standing, which is the ending the record will carry.
